Apartment interior plan

A Japandi apartment

Light oak, linen and paper lanterns, low seating, a projector instead of a TV, and plenty of built-in storage so the rooms stay calm. These are simple 3D sketches, not photo renders.

  • ≈ 85 m²
  • ceiling 2.63 m
  • full-height windows
  • 2 bedrooms → bedroom + tinker room
OverviewLivingKitchen & diningBedroomBathroomTinker roomBalcony
全体

The whole apartment

Kitchen, dining nook and living room share the balcony end. The bedroom and tinker room line the window wall, with the genkan, pantry, WC, laundry and bathroom along the hall.

居間

Living room and home cinema

A low L-sofa with a chaise and a kotatsu in front, so the sofa doubles as a backrest on the floor. Oak acoustic slats run behind it. The XGIMI projector sits on a turntable in an oak niche and throws onto the bedroom wall or the dining nook wall. Three paper lanterns hang outside the beam.

  • ≈ 17.5 m²
  • 113″ on the living wall
  • 91″ on the nook wall
  • sofa seat h 38 cm
台所

Kitchen and dining nook

A compact kitchen with a 2 m peninsula for extra worktop and storage. Behind it is a built-in booth with benches on four sides of a square table, like a raised tatami corner. It seats six.

  • kitchen ≈ 6 m²
  • nook ≈ 7 m²
  • peninsula 60 × 200
  • booth 175 × 175
  • table 90 × 90
寝室

Bedroom with a hidden walk-in

The bed is centred with the door swing kept clear. The walk-in is made of furniture, not walls: two cabinets with slatted oak backs face the bed, with a noren entrance at the window end. The one facing the bed is a shallow 22 cm closet for small things.

  • bedroom ≈ 11 m²
  • walk-in ≈ 3.4 m²
  • bed 160 × 200
風呂

Japanese-style bathroom

A dry room with a double vanity, mirror cabinet and tall cabinet. Behind a glass slider is a wet room where the whole floor can get wet: shower and hinoki stool first, then a soak in the tub.

  • dry room 2.6 m²
  • wet room 4.2 m²
  • vanity 140 cm, 2 basins
工房

Tinker, work-from-home and woodworking room

A 2 m desk for two along the bedroom wall, with the window kept clear. A sealed three-panel shoji closes off the workshop half, with an L-bench and pegboard, the 3D printer on a pull-out shelf, and a closet for the 10″ rack. A floor cushion by the window makes a crochet corner.

  • ≈ 10.2 m²
  • desk 200 × 72
  • bench 192 + 60 cm
  • shoji 3 × ≈ 68 cm
縁側

Balcony with a wisteria frame, plant wall and crops

Two low teak lounge chairs face the view across a teak table. The yakisugi planter along the glass railing gets the most sun, so it holds the crops.

Overhead is a freestanding oak frame in the style of a Japanese fujidana, built without drilling. Four posts against the side walls are clamped between floor and ceiling and carry the beams and slats. A classic Japanese wisteria in the far corner is trained along the front beam, where the light comes in. Two evergreen clematis cover the rest of the frame.

On the far wall, oak slats screwed to the posts form a plant wall with evergreen herbs and trailing ivy. A cedar-clad tank feeds drip lines to every planter.

  • ≈ 6.1 m²
  • crop planter 307 × 34, h 45
  • posts 4.5 × 9.5, floor to ceiling
  • beams at h 2.24
  • plant wall ≈ 155 × 210
三月

March: clematis in flower

The clematis flowers first, white and vanilla-scented across the whole canopy, while the wisteria is still bare. The winter crops are still in: leeks, kale and lamb's lettuce.

五月から夏

May to summer: wisteria in flower

The wisteria takes over with a purple curtain along the front beam. The planter switches to peas, bush tomatoes, strawberries, lettuce and basil. The renders show the crops fully grown, but the tomatoes and strawberries ripen in June and July.

冬

Winter: evergreen canopy

The wisteria is bare, but the clematis keeps the frame green and the herbs and ivy keep the wall green. Leeks, kale and lamb's lettuce fill the planter. The tank and drip lines are emptied for the frost.

Simplified block models to show layout, proportions and materials. Real finishes, fabrics and light will look softer.
